durableSession.standardSessionBody: Standard SSH sessions end when the connection drops. Durable sessions keep your shell state, running programs, and history alive through network changes, computer sleep, and Wave restarts.
durableSession.attachedBody: Your shell state, running programs, and history are protected. This session will survive network disconnects.
durableSession.detachedBody: Connection lost, but your session is still running on the remote server. Wave will automatically reconnect when the connection is restored.
durableSession.awaitingConnectionBody: Configured for a durable session. The session will start when the connection is established.
durableSession.awaitingStartBody: Configured for a durable session, but session hasn't started yet. Click below to start it manually.
durableSession.endedBody: The durable session has ended. This block is still configured for durable sessions.
durableSession.endedExitedBody: The shell was terminated and is no longer running. This block is still configured for durable sessions.
durableSession.endedLostBody: The session was lost or not found on the remote server. This may have occurred due to a system reboot or the session being manually terminated.
durableSession.failedToStartBody: The durable session failed to start.

onboarding.githubSupportBody: We're open source, open-model, and committed to providing a free terminal for individual users. Please show your support by giving us a star on
onboarding.communityBody: Get help, submit feature requests, report bugs, or just chat with fellow terminal enthusiasts.
onboarding.telemetryHint: Anonymous usage data helps us improve features you use.
onboarding.noProblemPrivacy: No problem, we respect your privacy.
onboarding.flyingBlind: But, without usage data, we're flying blind. A GitHub star helps us know Wave is useful and worth maintaining.

minor.waveAiIntro: Wave AI is your terminal assistant with full context. It can read your terminal output, analyze widgets, read and write files, and help you solve problems faster.
minor.newInV013Body: Wave AI now supports local models and bring-your-own-key! Use Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI-compatible provider.
minor.newInV014Body: Durable SSH sessions survive network drops, laptop sleep, and restarts — all without tmux or screen.
minor.thanksAdopter: Thanks for being an early Wave adopter! ⭐
minor.githubStarHint: A GitHub star shows your support for Wave (and open-source) and helps us reach more developers.

v0121.intro: Patch release focused on shell integration improvements, Wave AI enhancements, and restoring syntax highlighting in code editor blocks.
v0121.osc7Body: Wave now automatically tracks and restores your current directory across restarts for bash, zsh, fish, and pwsh shells
v0121.shellContextBody: Tracks when your shell is ready, last command executed, and exit codes for better terminal management
v0121.aiItem1: Display reasoning summaries while waiting for AI responses
v0121.aiItem2: Enhanced terminal context - AI now has access to shell state, current directory, command history, and exit codes
v0121.aiItem3: Added feedback buttons (thumbs up/down) for AI responses
v0121.aiItem4: Added copy button to easily copy AI responses to clipboard
v0121.otherItem1: Mobile user agent emulation support for web widgets
v0121.otherItem2: Fixed padding for header buttons in code editor
v0121.otherItem3: Restored syntax highlighting in code editor preview blocks

v0122.intro: Wave AI can now create and modify files with visual diff previews and easy rollback capabilities. Plus performance improvements and bug fixes.
v0122.fileWriteToolBody: Wave AI can now create and modify files with your approval
v0122.diffPreviewBody: See exactly what will change before approving edits
v0122.rollbackBody: Revert file changes with a simple "Revert File" button
v0122.aiItem1: Drag & drop files from preview viewer directly to Wave AI
v0122.aiItem3: Adjustable thinking level and max output tokens per chat
v0122.aiItem4: Improved tool descriptions and input validations
v0122.bugFixItem1: Fixed significant memory leak in the RPC system

v0123.intro: Wave AI model upgrade to GPT-5.1, new secret management features, and improved terminal input handling for interactive CLI tools.
v0123.gpt51Body: Upgraded to OpenAI's GPT-5.1 model for improved responses
v0123.thinkingModeBody: New dropdown to select between Quick, Balanced, and Deep thinking modes
v0123.aiItem3: Fixed path mismatch issue when restoring AI write file backups
v0123.inputHandlingBody: Better support for CLI tools like Claude Code
v0123.imagePasteBody: Paste images directly into terminal (saved to temp files)
v0123.terminalItem3: Shift+Enter now inserts newlines by default for multi-line commands
v0123.terminalItem4: Fixed duplicate text issue when switching input methods (IME)
v0123.secretWidgetBody: Store and manage sensitive credentials securely

v0130.intro: Wave v0.13 brings local AI support, bring-your-own-key (BYOK), a redesigned configuration system, and improved terminal functionality.
v0130.openaiCompatBody: Connect to Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter, and other local or hosted models
v0130.presetsBody: Built-in configs for OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Azure, and custom endpoints
v0130.multiModeBody: Easily switch between models and providers
v0130.newConfigBody: Dedicated widget accessible from the sidebar
v0130.betterOrgBody: Browse and edit settings with improved validation and error handling
v0130.integratedSecretsBody: Manage API keys and credentials from the config widget
v0130.bracketedPasteBody: Enabled by default for better multi-line paste behavior
v0130.windowsPasteBody: Ctrl+V now works as standard paste on Windows
v0130.sshPasswordBody: Store SSH passwords in Wave's secret store

v0131.intro: Wave v0.13.1 focuses on Windows platform improvements, Wave AI visual updates, and enhanced terminal navigation.
v0131.integratedLayoutBody: Cleaner interface with controls integrated into the tab-bar header
v0131.sshAgentBody: Improved SSH agent support on Windows
v0131.focusKeybindingBody: Wave AI focus key changed to Alt:0 on Windows
v0131.visualDesignBody: Complete UI refresh with transparency support for custom backgrounds
v0131.byokBody: Wave AI now works with bring-your-own-key and local models without requiring telemetry
v0131.scrollingKeybindingsBody: Added Shift+Home, Shift+End, Shift+PageUp, and Shift+PageDown for better navigation

v0140.intro: Wave v0.14 introduces Durable Sessions. Enable them to keep your remote sessions alive through network interruptions, computer sleep, and restarts — they'll automatically reconnect when your connection is restored.
v0140.sessionProtectionBody: Programs and shell state survive disconnects
v0140.stopGenerationBody: Ability to stop AI responses mid-generation
v0140.contextMenuBody: Quick access to splits, themes, and more
v0140.osc52Body: CLI apps can copy to system clipboard

v0141.intro: Wave v0.14.1 fixes several high-impact terminal bugs and adds new config options for focus, cursor style, and block navigation.
v0141.imeFixBody: Fixed Korean/CJK input losing or sticking characters
v0141.scrollResizeBody: Terminal stays at bottom across resizes
v0141.scrollbackSaveBodySuffix: command to save scrollback to a file
v0141.cursorStyleBody: Configure cursor shape and blink per-block
v0141.newProvidersBody: Added Groq and NanoGPT as built-in presets

v0142.intro: Wave v0.14.2 introduces a new block badge system for at-a-glance status, along with directory preview improvements and bug fixes. v0.14.3 is a patch release fixing a showstopper bug in onboarding.
v0142.badgesRollUpLabel: Block Badges Roll Up to Tabs
v0142.badgesRollUpBody: Blocks can display icon badges (with color and priority) that are visible in the tab bar for at-a-glance status
v0142.bellIndicatorBodyPrefix: Terminal bell badge now lights up the block and tab when your terminal rings (controlled by
v0142.wshBadgeBody: New command to set or clear badges from the CLI. Supports icons, colors, priorities, and PID-linked badges
v0142.claudeIntegrationBodySuffix: with Claude Code hooks to surface AI task status as tab bar notifications
v0142.dirPreviewBody: Improved mod time formatting, zebra-striped rows, better default sort, and YAML file support
v0142.bugfixNewWindow: [bugfix] Fixed "New Window" hanging on GNOME desktops
v0142.bugfixSaveSession: [bugfix] Fixed "Save Session As..." focused window tracking bug

v0144.intro: Wave v0.14.4 introduces vertical tabs, upgrades to xterm.js v6, and includes bug fixes and UI improvements.
v0144.verticalTabBody: Tabs can now be displayed vertically along the side of the window for more horizontal space. Toggle between horizontal and vertical layouts in settings.
v0144.xtermUpgradeBody: Improved terminal compatibility and rendering, resolving quirks with tools like Claude Code
v0144.macFirstClickBody: First click now focuses the clicked widget
v0144.configErrorsBody: Config errors to the WaveConfig view for less clutter
v0144.unsavedChangesWarning: WaveConfig now warns on Unsaved Changes
v0144.legacyAiRemoved: Deprecated legacy AI widget has been removed
v0144.bugfixFocus: [bugfix] Fixed focus bug for newly created blocks

v0145.intro: Wave v0.14.5 introduces a new Process Viewer widget, several quality-of-life improvements, and a fix for creating new config files from the Settings widget.
v0145.processViewerBody: New widget that displays running processes on local and remote machines, with CPU and memory usage and sortable columns.
v0145.quakeModeBodySuffix: now toggles a Wave window visible and invisible
v0145.splitButtonsSuffix: setting adds split buttons to block headers
v0145.toggleSidebar: Toggle the widgets sidebar on and off from the View menu
v0145.f2Rename: F2 to rename the active tab
v0145.mouseNavigation: Mouse back/forward buttons now navigate in web widgets
v0145.bugfixConfigFiles: Config files that didn't exist yet couldn't be created or edited from the Settings widget
